Use all your internet connections at the same time. Combine Wi-Fi, Ethernet and phone hotspots, so downloads, games and browsers get the speed of every connection added up.

A Mac with Wi-Fi + an Android phone. The menu shows both connections working at once. Watch the full 45-second video.
net-merge uses all your network adapters together. It works on Windows, macOS and Linux . It is free. There is no account, no server and no VPN.
A real test with Wi-Fi + an Android USB tether + an iPhone hotspot, 9 downloads at once: 232-303 Mbit/s . The fastest connection alone gave about 121 Mbit/s.
net-merge gives every new connection to one of your links. When an app opens many connections, they spread over all your links.
Good for: Steam and game downloads, browsers, system updates, cloud uploads (Google Drive), download managers like IDM, torrents.
Not for: one single connection. One connection always uses one link, so one big file from one connection does not get faster. Browsers can split a download into several connections; see the tip under Use it .
Works for every app , TCP and UDP, IPv4 and IPv6. You do not set up a proxy.
Smart: faster links get more connections. A link with no internet gets none until it works again.
Safe: if net-merge crashes, your internet keeps working.
Light: about 0.18 CPU cores per 100 Mbit/s.
macOS and Linux : paste this into a terminal.
Antivirus blocked it? Download net-merge-setup.exe and double-click it instead.
That's it: net-merge is installed and its icon appears in the menu bar or tray. On Linux the script uses your package manager (apt, dnf, zypper, apk or pacman) and on macOS Homebrew when you have it, so net-merge updates with the rest of your system. To start it at sign-in, tick Start at sign-in in its menu.
Want to choose the connection for each app? RoutEngine is the upgraded commercial version of net-merge, for Windows, macOS and Linux. Pick an adapter per app, add a fallback, and set a speed limit or data cap per app. Free for personal use, Pro for work.
Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, Raspberry Pi OS (apt):
Windows by hand : download net-merge-setup.exe and run it. Windows may warn because the app is not signed yet: click More info , then Run anyway . There is also a portable zip .
Then start it with net-merge tray (Linux, macOS) or from the Start menu (Windows).
Which CPUs: x86-64, ARM64 and Apple Silicon, ARMv7, ARMv6 (Raspberry Pi), x86 32-bit, RISC-V, PowerPC (ppc64le), s390x and LoongArch.
No password prompts: the Linux packages give net-merge the network rights it needs ( setcap ), and on macOS net-merge install adds one rule so that only net-merge tray can run as root without a password.
Linux tray icon: needs a desktop with StatusNotifierItem support: KDE, XFCE, Cinnamon, LXQt, Budgie, or GNOME with the AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem Support extension (Ubuntu already has it).
Firewall: if it blocks unknown traffic, trust the net-merge interface (for example firewall-cmd --zone=trusted --add-interface=net-merge ).
Signed repositories: apt, dnf, zypper and pacman use the key in packaging/apt-signing-key.asc , fingerprint 0168 C7AB 7772 1656 9048 11AE 904F 61E7 F4F1 C2A1 .
net-merge for Android uses Wi-Fi and mobile data at the same time. No root, no account, no server. It is new (beta).
On your phone, download net-merge-android.apk .
Open it and install it. If Android asks, allow your browser or file manager to install apps.
Open net-merge , tap the power button and tap OK on the VPN prompt.
Optional: add the net-merge tile to Quick Settings to turn it on and off with one tap.
Faster: apps that open many connections at once, like Play Store updates, web pages, torrents, cloud backups and download managers. One single download stays on one network, like on a computer.
Mobile data stays on while net-merge runs, so keep an eye on your data plan.
One VPN at a time: Android lets only one VPN app run, so net-merge can't run next to another VPN.
Problems? Open an issue and pick Android . The code is in net-merge/android .
macOS and Linux : paste this into a terminal. It stops net-merge and removes it the way it was installed (Homebrew, apt, dnf, zypper, apk, pacman or the download), with its repository and key.
Windows : paste this into PowerShell, or use Settings > Apps > Installed apps > net-merge > Uninstall .
Your network goes back to normal as soon as net-merge stops: it removes its virtual adapter and routes when it quits, and even after a crash.
Each block first stops the tray and turns off start at sign-in, then removes net-merge.
Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, Raspberry Pi OS (apt):
Windows portable zip : run net-merge.exe autostart off in its folder, quit the tray, then delete the folder.
NixOS : remove programs.net-merge (and the net-merge input) from your configuration and rebuild.
To try it without installing: sudo nix run github:net-merge/net-merge -- run .
net-merge needs two or more real connections. Use Wi-Fi plus one of these: a phone (USB tethering or hotspot), an Ethernet cable, or a second Wi-Fi. Plug it in and net-merge adds it within a few seconds. When you unplug it, its connections move to the others.
Windows and Linux: plug the phone in and turn on USB tethering (Android) or Personal Hotspot (iPhone). That is all.
Mac with an iPhone (nothing extra to install)
Plug the iPhone in with a cable. Tap Trust on the iPhone if it asks.
On the iPhone, open Settings > Personal Hotspot and turn on Allow Others to Join .
An iPhone USB network appears on the Mac. net-merge adds it in a few seconds.
Mac with an Android phone (needs the app TetherKit )
macOS cannot use Android USB tethering by itself. The app TetherKit adds that support.
Plug the phone in and turn on USB tethering in the phone's settings.
Click Apply in TetherKit. net-merge adds the new network in a few seconds.
Start net-merge first, then connect the Android phone. macOS drops the TetherKit connection each time net-merge starts or quits. Pausing and resuming is safe: net-merge keeps its virtual adapter while paused. If the phone link disappears, click Apply in TetherKit again. The iPhone is not affected.
A phone uses its mobile data, so part of your traffic goes through it while net-merge runs. Quit net-merge when you do not want that.
Start net-merge. A tray icon appears (menu bar on Mac).
The icon is green when it is merging and grey when it is paused.
It pauses by itself when fewer than two connections have internet, because there is nothing to merge, and the menu says Paused: one connection . It starts again by itself when a second connection works. If you pause or start it yourself, that choice wins: it will not start again after you paused it. Untick Pause when there is only one connection in the menu to switch this off, or run net-merge tray -auto-pause=false .
Hover the icon to see the speed of each connection and the total.
Right-click the icon (on Mac, click it) to open the menu. It shows each connection's speed, how many connections net-merge gave it, and the buttons Pause merging / Start merging and Quit . The line above Quit is the version you are running, like v0.3.3 . It reads the newest release number from GitHub (at start, and again every 6 hours) and turns into Update to v0.3.4 if there is one; click it to open the release page. Click a connection to cap it at 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 or 100 Mbit/s (or Unlimited ). For any other speed, from a terminal: net-merge limit "Ethernet 2" 25 (Mbit/s; 0 or unlimited removes the cap), and net-merge limit lists what is set. The cap covers its downloads and uploads and is remembered after a restart. Only traffic net-merge relays is capped: an app bound directly to an adapter (for example qBittorrent on a fixed interface) ignores it.
To start it at sign-in: tick Start at sign-in in the menu (or the box in the Windows installer, or run net-merge autostart on ). On a Mac this needs sudo net-merge install once.
Torrent clients already use every connection. Leave qBittorrent's network interface on Any interface .
Torrent clients already use every connection. Leave qBittorrent's network interface on Any interface .
Faster browser downloads. A browser downloads a file over one connection, so it uses one link. Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers can split it over several connections instead: Open chrome://flags/#enable-parallel-downloading (Edge: edge://flags/#enable-parallel-downloading , Brave: brave://flags/#enable-parallel-downloading ). Set Parallel downloading to Enabled and click Relaunch . Firefox has no such setting; for big files use a download manager, for example aria2c -x 8 -s 8 . Splitting only helps when the server allows downloading parts of a file, which most large download sites do.

net-merge list shows which connections are used and why others are skipped. net-merge status shows live numbers.

You only gain speed when each connection reaches the internet by its own path. Wi-Fi from your home router plus a phone on mobile data works. Wi-Fi and Ethernet plugged into the same router do not: they share one internet line, so the total stays the same.
Also remember that one connection always uses one link. Many parallel connections (Steam, browsers, download managers) are what speed up. Run net-merge status to see how many connections each link carries.
A VPN app on your computer (ProtonVPN, NordVPN and others) sends all your internet through itself. net-merge then has nothing to share, so nothing gets faster. Using the VPN on only one link is not safe either: anything sent over the other link skips the VPN.
Fix: set up the VPN on your routers instead, and turn the VPN app off on the computer. Most VPN providers have a guide for routers. net-merge then works as normal, and all your traffic still goes through the VPN.

Then update as normal ( sudo apt update , sudo dnf upgrade , sudo zypper refresh , sudo apk update or sudo pacman -Sy ).
Run net-merge list . It shows which connections are used and why the others are skipped, for example "no default gateway" (the link has no internet yet).
iPhone on a Mac: plug it in, tap Trust , and turn on Settings > Personal Hotspot > Allow Others to Join . If the iPhone USB network in System Settings > Network stays inactive, turn off its Disable unless needed switch.
Android on a Mac: install TetherKit and click Apply (see above).
Phone on Windows: if the phone does not appear in Network Settings , install your phone maker's USB driver.
macOS drops the TetherKit connection each time net-merge starts or quits (pausing and resuming is safe). Start net-merge first, then connect the phone. If it vanishes, click Apply in TetherKit again.
Windows can switch Wi-Fi off when Ethernet is plugged in. Open the Group Policy Editor ( gpedit.msc ), go to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > Windows Connection Manager , and set Minimize the number of simultaneous connections to the Internet or a Windows domain to Disabled .
The apps are not code-signed yet. On macOS run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine net-merge . On Windows click More info , then Run anyway .
net-merge only has something to do with two or more connections that have internet, so it waits. Plug in or connect the second one (see Add a second connection ) and it starts by itself after a few seconds. To merge anyway, choose Start merging (it then stays on until a second connection has come and gone), or untick Pause when there is only one connection .
Switching merging on or off cuts the connections that are open at that moment, which is why it waits 10 seconds with nothing moving before pausing (2 minutes if a download or upload is still going) and 3 seconds before resuming, and never switches by itself more than once every 30 seconds.
On Windows it may be behind the ^ arrow next to the clock. On macOS it is in the menu bar. On Linux the desktop needs StatusNotifierItem support (KDE, XFCE, Cinnamon, LXQt, Budgie, or GNOME with the AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem Support extension).
net-merge may use a different IP for each connection, and some sites tie your login to one IP. That is a limit of splitting connections over several links.
